title: Electrician (SSgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
2.     MOS 1141, Electrician (SSgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L

    a. Summary. Using knowledge of electrical theory and concepts,
electricians install, operate, maintain, and repair underground, above
ground, and tactical electrical power distribution systems. Additionally,
electricians perform preventive maintenance checks and service and operate
electrical power generation and power distribution equipment, load banks, and
floodlight sets. Electricians also install and repair interior wiring.
Corporals through staff sergeants are afforded the opportunity to attend a
skill progression course. The Advanced Electrician Course (M0311K2) provides
in-depth instruction on code requirements and planning electrical support to
include determining demand, phase balancing, and voltage drops. An
apprenticeship program, leading to U.S. Department of Labor certification as
a Journeyman Electrician, is available to electricians under the United
Services Military Apprenticeship Program (USMAP).

       b.    Prerequisites

             (1) Must have normal color vision.

             (2) Must possess an EL score of 90 or higher.

       c.    Requirements

        (1) Complete the Basic Electrician Course (M0311B2), Marine Corps
Engineer School, Camp Lejeune, NC.

        (2) Electricians corporals through staff sergeant must complete the
Advanced Electrician Course (M0311K2).

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (l), Marine Corps Engineer and Utilities Training and Readiness
Manual.

       e.    Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

             (1) Electricians 47-2111.

             (2) Electrical Power-Line Installers and Repairers 49-9051.

             (3) Power Distributors and Dispatchers 51-8012.

       f.    Related Military Skill.     None.

Prerequisites (1) Must have normal color vision. (2) Must possess an EL score of 90 or higher. c. nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
